own_solution.law: Timoshenko bimetal curvature: kappa = 6 dAlpha dT (1+m)^2 / (h [3(1+m)^2 + (1+mn)(m^2 + 1/(mn))]), m = t1/t2 = 1, n = E1/E2 = 2 (or 1/2, symmetric for m=1); cantilever with uniform curvature: delta = kappa L^2 / 2
assumptions: uniform temperature, constants independent of T
clamped segment flat; projecting part 20 cm curves uniformly
deflection magnitude (sign depends on which layer is on top, brass on convex side)

defect_reasons.other: The problem does not say which layer is on top, so only the magnitude (not the sign/direction) of the vertical deflection is determined; the asked 'vertical deflection' is naturally read as magnitude.

notes: kappa = 24*(7e-6*60)/(16.5*1e-3 m) = 0.6109 1/m; delta = 0.6109*0.2^2/2 = 12.22 mm. With projecting length 31 cm: delta = 0.6109*0.0961/2 = 29.35 mm. Variant sets: TB206/T6C9F both 14 mm (width, cancels); TE1D7/T1A9F/T374D/T9949 all 11 cm; T90F6/TC665 both 'a few centimetres' (non-numeric, both D, so no answer needed). T1A9F and T9949 assume the strip is re-clamped with 31 cm projecting after heating; since curvature is set by the uniform temperature, the newly exposed part curves the same way once released.
